title: Borrowing at a partner university library without exposing a loan history
moment: A National Taiwan University graduate student walks into National Chengchi University's library to borrow thesis references through the inter-university borrowing agreement. The desk wants to confirm she has no overdue or lost items at any partner library. Today staff look up her full cross-library borrowing record, which shows every title she has ever checked out, including sensitive topics.
predicate: Non-membership: the student's ID is not on the network's current list of patrons with overdue or lost items.
disclosed_today: Student ID, name, department, and a cross-library circulation view with titles, due dates and fine history.
issuer: The home university library, or the inter-library consortium, signing a periodically refreshed clean-standing credential.
why_zk: Good fit. The check is a single negative fact, and a non-membership proof against a signed delinquency list reveals nothing about what she borrowed. Weakness: the credential goes stale, so it needs a short validity window or a fresh revocation or list root, and the home library still sees which partner asked unless a presentation is made unlinkable.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the ALA library-records guidance, the library treats who-borrowed-what as confidential by policy; here, a non-membership proof plays that role by making the confidentiality technical, so the partner library never sees circulation records at all.

In the AEPD hotel case, the host records only the fields the registration rule requires rather than copying the whole ID; here, the proof of no overdue items plays that role by giving the desk only the one bit it needs instead of the full borrowing record.

title: Public library card upgrade for a member of a community reading cooperative
moment: A resident in Tainan joins a neighborhood book-sharing cooperative that lends from members' shelves and offers priority access to the city library's special collections. To admit new members, the cooperative coordinator asks them to bring a printout of their library account page, which shows current loans and holds, to prove they have no overdue or lost books elsewhere.
predicate: Non-membership: the member is not on the public library network's overdue or lost-item list.
disclosed_today: A screenshot or printout of the library account page with current loans, holds, reading history and fines, plus name and card number.
issuer: The municipal public library, which could sign a standing attestation through its app.
why_zk: Moderate. The volunteer needs no more than a clean-standing result, and a signed non-membership statement avoids handing over a reading history. The honest weakness is that the stakes are low and a volunteer group may simply trust a verbal statement or not care, so adoption depends on the library app offering this with no extra effort.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the ALA guidance, circulation records are confidential and not handed to outsiders; here, the signed clean-standing proof plays that role by keeping the account page away from the cooperative volunteer.

In the household register rule, the applicant shows an original for inspection and nothing is retained; here, presenting the credential from the phone plays that role, so the volunteer sees a valid result and keeps no copy.

title: School-to-university library access for a high schooler borrowing across the network
moment: A senior at a Taichung high school applies for a visiting-reader pass at a nearby university library to prepare a science fair project. The university asks the school librarian to send a note about the student, and the school pulls the student's full loan history to show nothing is overdue, which exposes interests and personal reading choices to staff at both institutions.
predicate: Non-membership: the student is not listed as having overdue or lost items in the school or public library network.
disclosed_today: Student name, school ID, a librarian-written letter, and often a printed loan history with titles and dates.
issuer: The school library, or the city public library system, signing the standing status on request.
why_zk: Moderate to weak. The privacy gain is real for a minor, since a loan history can reveal personal matters. The practical limit is that a school librarian can already vouch in a short letter, so a proof mainly helps by removing the temptation to attach the history, and it matters only if it is easy to issue and a university pass office will accept it.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In attorney-client privilege, a confidential exchange is damaged when an extra party is in the room; here, a minimal proof plays that role by keeping the school librarian and university staff from each learning more than the status requires.

In the telco case, the check used copyable identifiers and let a stolen identity pass; here, a signed credential bound to the student plays the contrasting role by making the claim hard to borrow or forge, unlike a bare ID number.
